_comment: WHAT EACH CODEC ACTUALLY DOES, per (route, content_type). Generated by
measurement, not by hand — see tests/codec_effectiveness.py, which is the
single definition shared by this file's generator and the guard that reads
it.
THESE RATIOS ARE NOT THE PUBLISHED COMPRESSION FIGURES AND MUST NEVER BE
QUOTED AS THEM. They are CHARACTER ratios taken through apply_codec at its
DEFAULT budget, chosen because that is stable and cheap enough to assert on
every run. The published figures are TOKEN ratios at a stated budget over a
stated corpus: prose measures 63.38% character reduction through the full
pipeline at budget 0.30, against the 18.47% recorded here for the same
route. Both are true; they answer different questions.
The RouteClass ratchet next door asks whether a codec EXISTS. This asks
whether it DOES ANYTHING, because apply_codec returns success=True with the
input unchanged and that is indistinguishable from a compression that saved
nothing.
THE UNIT IS (ROUTE, CONTENT TYPE) AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. At route
granularity log_compressor reads as effective at mean ratio 0.999, purely
because 8 stacktrace and mixed fixtures reach it and compress slightly. On
its own log content it returns the input unchanged on 15 of 15. A
route-level aggregate reports that codec as working.
measured_at_commit: 9122dab, except code_compressor/code which was remeasured at 115f134 after Vega ruling 72 moved it from inert to effective

effective._comment: success=True and at least one fixture came back shorter. A cell here that becomes inert is a REGRESSION and fails.

_comment: success=True on every fixture and never a byte shorter: the codec ran and
did nothing while reporting that it worked. THIS LIST MAY ONLY SHRINK.
Every entry carries a reason, because 'inert by design' and 'inert by
defect' look identical from the outside and only one of them is
publishable as a built codec.

log_compressor/log.reason: compress_logs folds templates recurring 3+ times. Every one of the 15 log fixtures is exactly 5 lines carrying 5 DISTINCT templates, so there is nothing to fold and the codec cannot fire by construction. The codec is sound; the corpus cannot exercise it. Real logs repeat heavily, so this is a generator defect and is the strongest single argument for the public-domain benchmark suite. BINDING CONSTRAINT (Atlas, 2026-08-09): do NOT resolve this by generating synthetic repeated-line fixtures so the codec fires. That would be the corpus defining the product — the exact disease the joint report diagnoses — and it would turn a real coverage gap into a green cell. This entry is retired only by measuring on real logs.

governance_safe_compression/incident_rep.reason: mapped to _passthrough in codecs/selector.py. Governance content is carried intact deliberately.

pii_redaction_before_compression/governa.reason: mapped to _passthrough. The open half has no PII path at all, so anchorization is unreachable — see the open-core seam ruling.

pii_redaction_before_compression/pii_mes.reason: mapped to _passthrough, as above. This is the single largest traffic group in the corpus and it compresses nothing.

reject_or_human_review/pii_message.reason: a refusal route. Compressing content routed for human review would defeat the routing.

reversible_retrieval_mode/retrieval_cont.reason: the abstention route by rule_router's own definition. Abstaining is the behaviour, not a failure to compress.

_comment: success=False — the route declines outright. Owned by the RouteClass
ratchet and its unbuilt_routes.json baseline; recorded here only so the
three buckets are exhaustive. This guard never rules on these, so the two
baselines cannot disagree about who owns a route.
